optimizedDescription.value: Define sole built-in SQLite `GraphStore`: dedicated-worker non-blocking ops, config-rooted persistence, atomic txns, FTS identity-aware search.

optimizedContext.value:
# SQLite Graph Store
## Rules
- `SQLiteGraphStore` implements `GraphStore` via `better-sqlite3`; semantics per `code-graph:graph-store`; stable backend id `sqlite`; sole built-in backend, selected when no explicit `graphStoreId`.
- All sync SQLite work (queries, mutations, txns, schema init, FTS, maintenance) runs inside dedicated persistent Node.js Worker Thread owned by open store; MUST NOT run on host event loop.
- One open store = exactly one persistent worker + one SQLite connection; no per-op workers/pooling; concurrent `open()`/`close()` share in-flight lifecycle Promise.
- Worker owns better-sqlite3 connection, prepared statements, transactions, schema work, FTS maintenance, backend fs work; native handles/prepared statements MUST NOT cross worker boundary.
- Host/worker communicate via strongly typed structured-cloneable request/result/error/progress DTOs with monotonic correlation ids; no functions/native objects/class instances across boundary.
- Worker processes ops through explicit FIFO serial queue; lifecycle, maintenance, reads, mutations never interleave.
- Host validates `maxPendingOperations >= 1`; default 256 outstanding; beyond limit rejects immediately `StoreOverloadError` without disturbing accepted work.
- `close()`: reject new work; drain accepted within `drainTimeoutMs` (default 5000ms); request worker-side db close; force terminate after graceful deadline; unsettled requests reject `StoreWorkerError`; await forced termination but never claim hard wall-clock bound during native execution.
- Runtime config crossing boundary uses serializable `SqliteRuntimeDescriptor`; custom `modulePath` MAY select compatible binding; internal worker-path test overrides not public options.
- Unexpected worker error/exit faults store + rejects outstanding with `StoreWorkerError`; recovery explicit `close()` then `open()`; never silent restart.
- `close()` starting while `open()` pending: shutdown owns final lifecycle state; `open()` MUST NOT publish open afterward.
- Bulk indexing via worker-side session `sessionId`; only session start creates state; staging/commit/rollback vs missing/finalized session reject; host enforces explicit active/committing/rolling-back/finished states bound to current store lifecycle generation.
- Progress callbacks observational; callback failures isolated, MUST NOT abort worker operation or txn.
- Closed-store recreation uses non-blocking host filesystem APIs for cleanup + storage-generation rotation.
- Batch symbol/relation queries = set-based worker ops; one batch call crosses boundary as ONE RPC, not per symbol/relation type; set-based predicates; incoming/outgoing relation lookup queries all requested symbol ids + relation types together; large input sets split into deterministic bounded SQL parameter chunks inside worker (SQLite param limits cannot fail valid traversal); preserve deterministic ordering + empty-input semantics of abstract contract.
- Exact batch node lookups (`getFilesByPaths`, `getDocumentsByPaths`, `getSpecsByIds`, `getSymbolsByIds`) = set-based worker ops; each logical batch crosses boundary once as one typed RPC, never per-node RPCs; `path IN (...)`/`id IN (...)` predicates; bounded SQL param chunks inside worker; dedupe repeated identities, omit unknown identities, preserve first requested-identity order; empty input returns empty array without RPC.
- Persistence rooted at project-level `configPath`: graph dir `{configPath}/graph`, scratch `{configPath}/tmp`; DB file + WAL/shared-memory companions only under derived dirs; create dirs on demand.
- Default backend role: durable persistence of file/document/symbol/spec/relation/meta state; atomic mutation semantics; full-text + identity-aware search for symbol/file/spec/document discovery; bulk indexing + full re-index; structured queries traversal/references/coverage/impact/hotspots/search/stats. Graph unreadable after backend change → full SQLite re-index = supported recovery path.
- Destructive recreation: discard all persisted SQLite graph data under `{configPath}/graph` incl WAL/SHM companions belonging to same root; rotate persisted storage-generation marker; ready for clean rebuild from scratch on reopen.
- Storage-generation sidecar under `{configPath}/graph` compatible with shared stale-detection contract (`graph/storage.epoch` acceptable); `open()` exposes current generation to owning provider; destructive recreation rotates generation so older open providers detect staleness and reopen.
- Adapter owns SQLite-specific persisted schema: files, symbols, specs, relations, FTS indexes, store metadata; derived/backend-specific columns OK (normalized search text); physical schema implementation concern; storage-agnostic consumers depend on `code-graph:graph-store`, not this spec.
- Persisted node kinds: `File` (incl source content for symbol snippet extraction), `Symbol`, `Spec`, `Document` (textual non-code), `Meta` records; File table includes source content for snippet derivation; Document table columns path (PK), configRelativePath, contentHash, content, workspace.
- Persisted relation families: IMPORTS DEFINES CALLS CONSTRUCTS USES_TYPE EXPORTS DEPENDS_ON COVERS_FILE COVERS_SYMBOL EXTENDS IMPLEMENTS OVERRIDES; physical layout adapter choice if observable GraphStore semantics preserved; COVERS_SYMBOL entries preserve relation metadata so stale symbol-level links survive reload.
- Search via FTS5 over symbol/spec/document incl Document content+paths; keep FTS MATCH candidate generation for `searchSymbols()`, `searchSpecs()`, `searchDocuments()`; sanitize + join multi-token queries with OR for broad discovery; expand raw tokens via shared specd/code-aware lexical policy before identity-aware ranking; supplement FTS candidates with identity-derived candidates when tokenization misses strong identity hit required by abstract contract.
- Identity-aware ranking in SQL explicit ordering columns (computed rank columns/CASE), not BM25 weights alone: boost exact canonical identity matches (Spec ID, Symbol Name/ID, Document Path); strong non-exact identity matches ahead generic content-only (symbol declared-name equality vs comment/body-only hits; spec-id prefix/suffix/substring/component matches; document canonical-path/config-relative-path prefix/suffix/substring/component matches); count expanded query tokens matching selected identity fields, rank higher coverage above lower when intent competing; BM25 ranks remaining textual matches after identity preference applied.
- Observable ordering: exact canonical identity first > identity-oriented non-exact hits > body/comment/content-only; exact token > prefix token > suffix token > arbitrary substring token; real identity-component match beats substring-only same identity field; more expanded identity-token coverage outranks fewer when relevance otherwise competing; generic term frequency in spec/document body MUST NOT outrank stronger spec-id/symbol-name/document-path match for same query intent.
- FTS schema: `symbol_fts` (Symbol.name, Symbol.comment), `spec_fts` (Spec.title, Spec.description, Spec.content), `document_fts` (Document.path, Document.content); stemming/weighted BM25/identity boost unions/other SQLite ranking options allowed if abstract graph-store contract satisfied; ranking expressed via explicit SQL ordering logic over discovered candidate set; candidate discovery MAY combine FTS MATCH results + identity-derived candidates; MUST NOT replace FTS retrieval with plain whole-query LIKE filtering only.
- Derive match-aware snippets + 1-based line range from persisted file source content or FTS matches; persisted File content used for snippet extraction SHALL NOT become separate full-text searchable file category.
- Transactions execute entirely inside worker preserving atomic mutation semantics; txn MUST NOT span multiple host/worker round trips; each atomic mutation incl `upsertFile()`, `removeFile()`, `upsertSpec()`, `removeSpec()`, bulk commit = one self-contained worker operation; failure preserves previously committed graph state.
- Bulk indexing stages data to worker-side session in bounded chunks, never one repository-sized structured-clone payload; commit makes complete session visible atomically in one SQLite transaction; reference-fact chunks merge with earlier chunks from same session; worker emits serializable progress stages cleanup/files/documents/symbols/specs/reference facts/observations/relations/search indexes forwarded to optional observational callback; prepared statements/temp tables/bounded SQL chunks MAY keep run stable; scratch artifacts stay under `{configPath}/tmp`.
- Schema versioning: track backend-specific schema version; on open execute current SQLite schema definition → verify/record current version in persisted metadata → prepare required FTS structures; incompatible persisted version MAY require destructive rebuild rather than incremental migration.
- Backend-specific companion files (WAL, shared-memory) MAY exist next to primary DB file; implementation detail, not part abstract GraphStore contract.
- Reference schema upgrade: persist logical-symbol, declaration, member, symbol-space, binding, provenance, coverage, construct-range, selection-range fields required by `GraphStore`; structured lookup columns indexed; serialized canonical ids MUST NOT be parsed or substring-ranked for semantic lookup; canonical ids remain unique external identities; backend-local integer row keys MAY join physically if provider-visible ids unchanged.
- Substring-capable source-content index + bounded short-query fallback per abstract store; reverse coverage + new traversal batch reads use set-based predicates + deterministic ordering.
- Track reference schema version `9`; later schema-affecting change increments exactly once; incompatible data rejects ordinary reads; `graph index` rebuilds destructively, rotates `storage.epoch`, rebuilds search indexes before readiness.
- Incremental-hydration state persists: indexed-input observations, freshness latches, VCS evidence, compact unchanged-file facts; one indexing run = one transaction, set-based endpoint validation, bounded writes, one commit, one semantic/content index rebuild.
## Constraints
- Infrastructure adapter, not part of abstract graph-store contract.
- `sqlite` stable backend id selecting this adapter from multi-backend graph-store registry.
- SQLite-specific file layout, FTS behavior, schema shape, schema-version handling defined here, not `code-graph:graph-store`.
- All SQLite scratch files + persisted database artifacts rooted under configPath.
- Storage-agnostic use cases + CLI commands MUST NOT depend on this spec unless truly requiring SQLite-specific behavior.
